why_not_one_ladder_per_target: all 32 remaining cells carry distinct (a,bb,e,h) shapes, so a same-shape ladder serves exactly one target
grouping_rule: within a b level, group by which of bb/e/h are nonzero; those flags are restrictions that change the domination relation, while a and d vary inside a group

groups.serves: one rung at this shape dominates the states of every member, because each member's states are bounded componentwise by the member and the shape is the componentwise max over members
groups.caveat: a larger shape carries a larger capacity and therefore a weaker bound; whether the shared ladder prunes enough is measured, not assumed
